purpose: Bounded research-only follow-up: timely siege prerequisites, positive capture control, and symmetric difficulty

timelySiegeMatchedCase.finding: Prioritising the already-legal dependency chain after a recorded fortified target moves redstone 74->61, engineering 87->74, and catapult queue 99->86. It does not produce a capture or conquest victory; the rival still wins Industrial one round earlier. This supports late siege access as a real bottleneck without claiming it is the sole cause.

bothArms.attackType: melee move into city with ownership transfer

capturePositiveControl.finding: With the visible target wall already at zero but one defender present, the ordinary AI uses the shared legal action/combat path and captures on round 3. This is a positive ownership-transfer gate, not evidence that the fortified siege path works.

fortifiedSiegeNegativeControl.finding: The existing fortified fixture still produces no wall damage in eight actual turns; this is a negative diagnostic of the current scenario/controller path, not a claim that Combat.damage or city capture is broken.

symmetricDifficulty.finding: Both-player Deity does not grant visible economy/combat bonuses and, in these two matched cases, does not improve the conquest seat's research or city count. The 75123 case is exactly identical on conquest progress; 95117 differs only slightly in terminal timing and opponent actions. This is evidence about these deterministic cells, not a global difficulty ranking.

limitations: The timely-siege comparison is one deterministic seed/seat with the same live opponent and research-only score changes.
The positive control starts after the wall-breach requirement and therefore cannot validate fortified siege timing.
The symmetric difficulty sample contains two matched seed/seat cases; it should not be generalized to all maps, civilizations or victory goals.
No gameplay costs, stats, movement, visibility or victory rules were changed.
